title: Conserved water molecules as structural ligands modulating pathogenic variation in human protein binding sites
authors: Janez Konc; Karmen Recer; Tanja Kunej; Dušanka Janežič
one_liner_zh: 该文研究保守水分子作为结构配体影响人类蛋白结合位点致病突变，虽涉及蛋白-配体结合和MD模拟，但核心对象非蛋白质-DNA互作，且未涉及TF-DNA体系或核酸结合建模，仅方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: Conserved water molecules (CWMs) are tightly bound solvent molecules that occupy well-defined and recurrent positions in protein structures. Although they are known to influence protein stability, function, and ligand binding, their contribution to human genetic disease has remained largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that CWMs substantially contribute to the pathogenicity of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). By systematically mapping SNPs onto ligand-binding and conserved water sites across human protein structures in the Protein Data Bank, we find that pathogenic variants are strongly enriched at CWM positions. Enrichment is particularly pronounced at CWM sites within ligand-binding regions, exceeding that observed for ligand-binding sites as a whole. To establish a mechanistic link, we performed molecular dynamics simulations on human lysosomal acid glucosylceramidase (GCase), encoded by GBA1 and associated with Gaucher disease and Parkinson’s disease risk. Removal of a single conserved water molecule in the wild-type protein recapitulates key structural features of the pathogenic L444P variant, whereas stabilization of this water in the mutant restores native-like behavior. These findings demonstrate that disruption of a conserved water molecule can induce long-range structural changes consistent with disease-associated mutations. Together, our results identify conserved water molecules as functional structural elements whose disruption represents a recurrent mechanism of protein dysfunction and provide direct mechanistic evidence for their pathogenic role in Gaucher disease. Significance Statement Are conserved water molecules hidden determinants of human genetic disease? By systematically mapping single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) onto protein structures, we show that pathogenic variants are strongly enriched at conserved water positions, particularly within ligand-binding sites. This enrichment exceeds that observed for most previously studied ligand types, including small molecules, nucleic acids, and proteins. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that disruption of a single conserved water molecule can induce long-range structural effects consistent with disease-associated variants in lysosomal acid glucosylceramidase, linking these findings to Gaucher disease and Parkinson’s disease risk. Together, our results establish conserved water molecules as previously underappreciated structural determinants of human disease and highlight their relevance for understanding genetic variation and guiding drug discovery.
abstract_zh: 保守水分子（CWMs）是紧密结合的溶剂分子，在蛋白质结构中占据明确且重复出现的位置。尽管已知它们影响蛋白质稳定性、功能和配体结合，但它们对人类遗传疾病的贡献在很大程度上仍未得到探索。在此，我们证明CWMs显著贡献于单核苷酸多态性（SNPs）的致病性。通过系统地将SNPs映射到蛋白质数据库（Protein Data Bank）中人类蛋白质结构的配体结合位点和保守水分子位点上，我们发现致病性变异在CWM位置显著富集。这种富集在配体结合区域内的CWM位点尤为突出，超过了整个配体结合位点所观察到的富集程度。为建立机制联系，我们对人溶酶体酸性葡萄糖神经酰胺酶（GCase）进行了分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟，该酶由GBA1编码，与戈谢病和帕金森病风险相关。在野生型蛋白质中移除单个保守水分子重现了致病性L444P变体的关键结构特征，而在突变体中稳定该水分子则恢复了类似天然的行为。这些发现表明，破坏一个保守水分子可诱导与疾病相关突变一致的长程结构变化。综合来看，我们的结果将保守水分子识别为功能性结构元件，其破坏代表了蛋白质功能障碍的一种反复出现的机制，并为其在戈谢病中的致病作用提供了直接机制证据。意义声明：保守水分子是否是人类遗传疾病的隐藏决定因素？通过将单核苷酸多态性（SNPs）系统映射到蛋白质结构上，我们表明致病性变异在保守水分子位置显著富集，尤其是在配体结合位点内。这种富集超过了大多数先前研究的配体类型（包括小分子、核酸和蛋白质）所观察到的程度。分子动力学模拟进一步揭示，破坏单个保守水分子可诱导与溶酶体酸性葡萄糖神经酰胺酶中疾病相关变体一致的长程结构效应，将这些发现与戈谢病和帕金森病风险联系起来。综合来看，我们的结果确立了保守水分子作为人类疾病中先前未被充分认识的结构决定因素，并强调了它们在理解遗传变异和指导药物发现中的相关性。
